sources.text:
Peričnik Falls (pronounced [pɛˈɾiːtʃnik]; Slovene: slap Peričnik) is a waterfall in Triglav National Park, Slovenia. The waterfall consists of two distinct cascades: the 16-metre Upper Peričnik Falls and the more dramatic 52-metre Lower Peričnik Falls, with both heights recently confirmed through precise geodetic measurements. A notable feature is the ability to walk behind the curtain of the lower waterfall, making it one of the most photographed natural attractions in the Julian Alps. The falls were first made accessible to visitors in 1895, when the local priest and mountaineer Jakob Aljaž cleared debris and constructed the initial footpath.


== Name ==
The name Peričnik (in the local dialect also Perečnik) is ultimately derived from the verb prati, which originally meant 'to strike, beat'. It also refers to water falling over a steep cliff (cf. also Peračica), and in standard Slovene has also developed into the sense 'to wash clothing' (via the sense 'to beat laundry').


== Description ==
Peričnik Falls is one of the best-known waterfalls in Slovenia. It flows from a hanging valley in Triglav National Park into the glacial Vrata Valley, where the water of Peričnik Creek then flows...

stops.name: Peričnik Falls
stops.detail: Peričnik Falls ist ein Wasserfall im Triglav Nationalpark, Slowenien. Der Wasserfall besteht aus zwei verschiedenen Kaskaden: dem 16-Meter-Oberen Peričnik Falls und dem dramatischeren 52-Meter-Unteren Peričnik Falls, wobei beide Höhen kürzlich durch präzise geodätische Messungen bestätigt wurden. Ein bemerkenswertes Merkmal ist die Fähigkeit, hinter dem Vorhang des unteren Wasserfalls zu gehen, was ihn zu einer der am meisten fotografierten Naturattraktionen der Julischen Alpen macht. Die Wasserfälle wurden erstmals 1895 für Besucher zugänglich gemacht, als der örtliche Priester und Bergsteiger Jakob Aljaž Trümmer räumte und den ersten Fußweg baute.
